You should go to the website for the manufacturer for all the different components and download the latest drivers from their website. Then go to the Control Panel > Device Managers and go through the devices listed, right click them and go to Properties to check which driver is installed. If it is not the one you downloaded from the website then click "Update Driver", then click "Browse my computer for driver software" and navigate to the folder where you stored the driver that you downloaded for that device. Don't forget to download the driver package for your motherboard too.

If your graphics still look shitty after updating things then you might have a problem where you computer is using the gpu that's onboard the motherboard or the processor instead of your dedicated gpu card. I don't remember how to switch that but you should be able to google it up easily enough.

You'll need to go into the BIOS if you need to switch the graphics card. Usually it's del when booting up on some systems F1, it says what to push when booting up. It's a good idea to take a look in any case on a new system to make sure your boot sequence is right and all drives and ram etc are listed.
